status: exact local Mertens-path DCT transference with an isolated generic first-mode barrier and one open two-component gate

rows.statement: For 0<alpha<1 set q_n=mu(n)n^(-1-alpha), r_N=sum_(n>N)q_n, and R_alpha=sum_(N>=1)N^alpha|r_N|^2.
rows.proof_boundary: These are the checked reciprocal-Mobius tail coordinates.

rows.statement: For dyadic K let y_j=r_(K+j-1), 1<=j<=K, and let c_(K,r)=<y,phi_r> in the Neumann DCT basis.
rows.proof_boundary: The basis phi_r and its high-mode estimate are those of Lemma 11.22V.

rows.statement: Define T_(K,m)=sum_(ell=1)^m q_(K+ell)=r_K-r_(K+m), 0<=m<=K, with T_(K,0)=0, and set z_j=T_(K,j-1), 1<=j<=K.
rows.proof_boundary: T is the origin-anchored reciprocal-weighted Mobius path inside the dyadic annulus.

rows.statement: The tail vector is exactly y_j=r_K-z_j.
rows.proof_boundary: This keeps the incoming tail level and the local path in one affine identity; neither term may be discarded.

rows.statement: Let tau_(K,r)=<z,phi_r>, 0<=r<K.
rows.proof_boundary: This is an orthonormal DCT of the K-vector (T_(K,0),...,T_(K,K-1)).

rows.statement: c_(K,0)=sqrt(K)r_K-tau_(K,0), while c_(K,r)=-tau_(K,r) for 1<=r<K.
rows.proof_boundary: The nonconstant DCT vectors have zero sum; the constant vector has inner product sqrt(K) with the all-ones vector.

rows.statement: For 1<=r<K, c_(K,r)=-sqrt(2/K)sum_(m=1)^(K-1)T_(K,m)cos(pi*r*(m+1/2)/K).
rows.proof_boundary: Discrete summation by parts in the sine formula of Lemma 11.22V cancels its 1/sin(pi*r/(2K)) factor exactly.
Combine row 6 with DCT Parseval.
The nonconstant modes are exactly the centered local-path energy, not merely bounded by it.

rows.statement: After deleting the constant DCT row and the fixed column T_(K,0)=0, the (K-1)-square transform has Gram matrix I_(K-1)-K^(-1)11^T.
rows.proof_boundary: Restrict the full identity sum_(r>=1)phi_r phi_r^T=I-K^(-1)11^T.

rows.statement: The deleted transform has singular values 1 with multiplicity K-2 and K^(-1/2) with multiplicity 1.
rows.proof_boundary: The all-ones direction has Gram eigenvalue 1/K; its orthogonal complement has eigenvalue 1.

rows.statement: With R_K=ceil(sqrt(K)), R_alpha<infinity iff sum_(K dyadic)K^alpha(|sqrt(K)r_K-tau_(K,0)|^2+sum_(1<=r<R_K)|tau_(K,r)|^2)<infinity.
rows.proof_boundary: Rows 6 and 8 rewrite the exact low-mode criterion of Lemma 11.22V; its high modes remain automatically summable.

rows.statement: For any fixed cofinal alpha_j->0 in (0,1), RH is equivalent to the path criterion in row 12 for every alpha_j.
rows.proof_boundary: This composes row 12 with the checked cofinal R_alpha criterion and does not prove the displayed series finite.

rows.statement: The surviving target has two components: the affine mean defect sqrt(K)r_K-tau_(K,0), and the first O(sqrt(K)) nonconstant DCT coefficients of the local path.
rows.proof_boundary: Control of only one component does not algebraically control the other.

rows.statement: Let S_(K,m)=M(K+m)-M(K)=sum_(ell=1)^m mu(K+ell), and a_m=(K+m)^(-1-alpha).
rows.proof_boundary: S is the ordinary local Mertens-increment path on the same anchored annulus.

rows.statement: For 1<=m<=K, T_(K,m)=a_m S_(K,m)+sum_(ell=1)^(m-1)S_(K,ell)(a_ell-a_(ell+1)).
rows.proof_boundary: This is finite Abel summation applied to sum a_ell(S_ell-S_(ell-1)).

rows.statement: With b_m=1/a_m, S_(K,m)=b_m T_(K,m)+sum_(ell=1)^(m-1)T_(K,ell)(b_ell-b_(ell+1)).
rows.proof_boundary: Sum (T_ell-T_(ell-1))/a_ell. The correction is negative because b_m is increasing.

rows.statement: For the vectors 1<=m<K, ||T_K||_2<=(2+alpha)K^(-1-alpha)||S_K||_2.
rows.proof_boundary: Use a_m<=K^(-1-alpha), a_ell-a_(ell+1)<=(1+alpha)K^(-2-alpha), and the strict-prefix operator norm <=K.

rows.statement: For the same vectors, ||T_K||_2>=[2^alpha(3+alpha)]^(-1)K^(-1-alpha)||S_K||_2.
rows.proof_boundary: Apply row 17 with b_m<=(2K)^(1+alpha), b_(ell+1)-b_ell<=(1+alpha)(2K)^alpha, and prefix norm <=K.

rows.statement: Rows 18-19 compare full local paths only; the triangular Abel transform does not commute with projection onto the first O(sqrt(K)) DCT modes.
rows.proof_boundary: A full-path norm equivalence cannot be promoted to a low-mode estimate without a separate commutator or signed arithmetic argument.

rows.statement: For fixed alpha and every dyadic K>=4 set A_K=2^(-2-alpha)pi^(-1)K^(-alpha), T*_(K,m)=A_K sin(2pi*m/K), and q*_(K+m)=T*_(K,m)-T*_(K,m-1).
rows.proof_boundary: Set q*_1=0. The disjoint annuli (K,2K] define one global scalar sequence; it is not the Mobius sequence.

rows.statement: |q*_n|<=n^(-1-alpha), and the sequence is absolutely summable because each dyadic block has l1 norm <=2pi*A_K.
rows.proof_boundary: Use |sin u-sin v|<=|u-v| and n<=2K; sum_(K dyadic)K^(-alpha)<infinity.

rows.statement: Every block has sum_(K<n<=2K)q*_n=0; hence r*_K=0 at every dyadic endpoint, tau*_(K,0)=0, and c*_(K,0)=0.
rows.proof_boundary: T*_(K,K)=T*_(K,0)=0 and the complete discrete sine sum over m=0,...,K-1 vanishes.

rows.statement: |c*_(K,1)|=A_K sqrt(2/K) cos(pi/K)/2 times [csc(pi/(2K))+csc(3pi/(2K))].
rows.proof_boundary: Use product-to-sum and the finite sine-sum formula on sin(2pi*m/K)cos(pi*(m+1/2)/K).

rows.statement: For K>=4, |c*_(K,1)|>=A_K sqrt(K)/pi and therefore K^alpha|c*_(K,1)|^2>=2^(-4-2alpha)pi^(-4)K^(1-alpha); the dyadic series diverges although row 23 holds.
rows.proof_boundary: Use cos(pi/K)>=sqrt(2)/2 and sin x<=x. Since alpha<1, the lower-bound terms do not even tend to zero.

rows.statement: Coefficient size, absolute convergence, zero dyadic endpoint tails, and zero block mean cannot control the first nonconstant mode by a generic Hilbert-space or large-sieve argument.
rows.proof_boundary: Rows 21-25 are a generic scalar countermodel only. They show that Mobius-specific signed cancellation is necessary but do not describe the actual Mobius coefficients.

rows.statement: Davenport gives the uniform arbitrary-log estimate for sum_(n<=X)mu(n)e(n theta); Zhang records this and quotes power refinements under a zero-free half-plane hypothesis for every Dirichlet L-function.
rows.proof_boundary: These sources support the logarithmic unconditional bound and the stated conditional calibrations, not the open path series.

rows.statement: At the quoted all-Dirichlet zero-free endpoint a=1/2, the Baker-Harman/Zhang uniform exponent is 3/4+epsilon; the threshold from Lemma 11.22V then closes only alpha>1/2+2epsilon, not a cofinal alpha->0 sequence.
rows.proof_boundary: This is exponent bookkeeping for that theorem, not a claim that stronger conditional or future methods are impossible.

rows.statement: The unconditional Maier-Sankaranarayanan rational estimate quoted by Zhang retains Dirichlet-L zero-density terms; the focused source audit found no supported simplification to the uniform cofinal-closing power needed here.
rows.proof_boundary: This is a focused search report, not a novelty, priority, or exhaustive-literature claim.

rows.statement: A viable Vaughan or bilinear attack must act on mu before rowwise absolute values and preserve signed coupling across the low modes and scales; bounding the full local S path after row 19 merely recycles the Mertens-energy target.
rows.proof_boundary: The exact transference identifies where a pre-collapse arithmetic gain must enter but supplies no such gain.

rows.statement: Translation averages, almost-all short-interval theorems, and estimates for only the nonzero rational phases do not automatically control both components in row 14; this reduction also concerns R_alpha rather than the full Burnol energy Q.
rows.proof_boundary: Each promotion requires an explicit de-averaging, mean-mode, or full-Q implication already absent from the proof.

rows.statement: For every alpha in one fixed cofinal sequence, prove dyadic summability of the affine mean defects and the first ceil(sqrt(K))-1 nonconstant local-path DCT modes in row 12, using Mobius-specific signed cancellation.
rows.proof_boundary: This remains RH-equivalent. No low-mode power gain, RH, PF-infinity, or Lambda<=0 is proved.
